description:
Helping Hands app becomes a design viewer first: on launch, open straight to the newest design with no menus to get through first.

Jake's words: "Also update Helping Hands too. When we drop a new design on there, when we first land in the app, we should be able to see that design directly. Helping Hands right now should just be a design viewer platform. So we should see the first item right there."

Spec:
- On launch the app opens directly to the newest design (e.g. the 3D gripper model from pebble voice-6d8b9fd8: rendered 3D model/STL viewer with rotate/zoom, plus its images). No menus first.
- When an agent drops a new design into the repo, it shows up as the first item the next time the app opens (or live).
- Other designs are reachable by swiping or a simple list.

results.identified_issue: Design = folder under cad/ containing renderable/STEP files directly, or its parent when the folder is named export/ or out/ (Scripts/stage_cad_models.py find_designs; skips render/, tools/, __pycache__, dot-dirs incl .venv). Newest = git log -1 %ct over the export + render dirs, falling back to file mtime if uncommitted. Primary model = largest file with 'assembly' in name and not 'open', else largest mesh. Manifest gains a 'designs' array; models' 'engine' is now the design's README heading (ModelViewerScreen groups by it). Swipe is a DragGesture on the lower ScrollView only (simultaneousGesture), deliberately not a paged TabView, because SceneKit camera drags would fight page swipes. If the design names read too long, split happens on the em dash in CADDesign.title/subtitle. Unverified on device: gesture feel, Picker look on macOS, the 17 MB bundle growth (renders, incl. 900 KB Blender PNGs).
results.summary: Helping Hands now opens straight to the newest design: the hand gripper loads in a 3D viewer you can rotate and zoom, with its renders underneath. Swipe or use the list for older designs.
results.detailed_description:
When you open the app, the newest design is already on screen. Right now that's the hand gripper from voice-6d8b9fd8. The top half is the 3D model: drag to rotate, pinch to zoom, and the scope button resets the view. It opens on the closed assembly. Below that you get the design's name and date, a Part picker for the other STLs (upper jaw, thumb cup, pads), and every render at full width. Tap a render to see it bigger.

To see other designs, swipe sideways on the lower half, or tap the list button in the top-left. Swiping on the 3D model rotates the model instead, so the two don't conflict. Six designs show up: hand gripper, crow beak, the build123d, Blender and OpenSCAD grippers, and the SO-101 reference. The arm info, plan listener and 3D-file browser moved behind the wrench button ("Workshop").

How new designs show up: you don't register anything by hand. The build step scans cad/ for any folder with STL/OBJ/STEP files, either loose or in an export/ or out/ subfolder. It takes the renders from render/, uses the README's first heading as the name, and sorts by the last commit that touched the exports or renders. So when an agent pushes a new design, it's the first screen on the next build Vigil installs. It doesn't update live while the app is open, because the files are bundled at build time. Side effects: before this, the hand gripper and crow weren't in the app at all because the old script had a hardcoded folder list. The app is also about 10 MB bigger because it now bundles the PNG renders.

Not run on a device. I didn't build. Both iOS and macOS typecheck cleanly, and I ran the staging script by hand, which found the 6 designs with hand_gripper first.

summary: Helping Hands should open straight to the newest design, such as the 3D gripper STL viewer with rotate and zoom, instead of menus. New designs dropped into the repo should appear first on next open, with older designs reachable by swiping or a simple list.
